Rashi on Eruvin 35a:10:1.hebrew: אלא לצורך תשמישן - ועיקר תשמישו של סכין לא לחתוך חבלים הוא, אלא לחם ובשר ואוכלין. והכי פליגי: תנא קמא לית ליה דרבי נחמיה, הלכך עירובו עירוב, דפסיק ליה למיתנא. רבי אליעזר אומר: אם בעיר אבד — הרי זה עירוב, דכי מדכר ליה מייתי ליה דרך קרפיפות; ואם בשדה — אינו עירוב, דמיפסיק מנעול לא מצי, כדרבי נחמיה:
Rashi on Eruvin 35a:10:1.english: Only for the purpose of their use - And the primary use of a knife is not to cut ropes, but rather bread, meat, and food. And this is how they disagree: The first tanna does not hold in accordance with Rabbi Neḥemya; therefore, his eiruv is a [valid] eiruv, as he can cut the cord. Rabbi Eliezer says: If [the key] was lost in the town, it is a [valid] eiruv, because when he remembers [where it is], he can bring it via enclosures [karpeifot]; and if [it was lost] in the field, it is not a [valid] eiruv, as he is not able to cut [open] the lock, in accordance with [the view of] Rabbi Neḥemya.

Rashi on Eruvin 35a:11:1.hebrew: נתגלגל חוץ לתחום אינו עירוב - הואיל ויש מביתו שהוא לן שם עד עירובו יותר מאלפים אמה, דממה נפשך, כל היכא דקנה שביתה — אי בביתו, אי בעירובו — לא מצי למיזל ולמשקליה:
Rashi on Eruvin 35a:11:1.english: [If] it rolled beyond the Shabbat limit, it is not an eiruv - Since from his house, where he is spending the night, to his eiruv there is more than two thousand cubits; for whichever way you look at it, wherever he acquired [his Shabbat] residence — whether in his house or at his eiruv — he cannot go and take it.

Rashi on Eruvin 35a:11:2.hebrew: נפל עליו גל - מפרש בגמ' דבעי מרא וחצינא לפנויי, דהויא מלאכה ולא שבות:
Rashi on Eruvin 35a:11:2.english: A pile [of stones] fell on it - It is explained in the Gemara that it requires a hoe and a pickaxe to clear it, which is [prohibited] labor and not [merely] a rabbinic decree.

Rashi on Eruvin 35a:11:3.english: Teruma and it became ritually impure - For it is not fit, neither for him nor for others.

Rashi on Eruvin 35a:11:4.hebrew: משחשיכה - כבר קנה עירוב בין השמשות, ושבת — הואיל והותרה, הותרה:
Rashi on Eruvin 35a:11:4.english: After dark - He had already acquired [his residence through the] eiruv at twilight; and [regarding] Shabbat, since it was permitted, it remains permitted.

Rashi on Eruvin 35a:12:1.hebrew: ספק - אם מבעוד יום, אם משחשיכה:
Rashi on Eruvin 35a:12:1.english: In doubt - Whether [it was] while it was still day, [or] whether after nightfall.

Rashi on Eruvin 35a:12:2.hebrew: הרי זה חמר גמל - דמספקא לן: אי קני ליה זה עירוב והכא הוי ביתו, ומהכא יש לו אלפים אמה לכל רוח והפסיד אלפים שמעבר ביתו; או שמא לא קנה עירוב, ומביתו יש לו אלפים לכל רוח ולא קנה לעבר עירובו כלום. ומחמת ספק זה, נאסר לילך אלא אלפים אמה שבין ביתו לעירובו, דממה נפשך בהנך משתרי; אבל אלפים שמעירובו ואילך — לא, דילמא לא קנה עירוב, ומביתו ואילך נמי לא — דלמא קנה עירוב. נמצא, זה מושכו כאן לילך וזה מושכו לכאן, כאדם המנהיג חמור וגמל, שהחמור הולך לפניו וזה מנהיגו, והגמל הוא מושך, וצריך לפנות לפניו ולאחריו:
Rashi on Eruvin 35a:12:2.english: This person is a donkey driver [and] a camel driver - For it is in doubt to us whether this eiruv acquired [his Shabbat residence] for him and here is his home, and from here he has two thousand cubits in every direction, but he forfeited the two thousand [cubits] that are beyond his house; or perhaps he did not acquire [a residence through the] eiruv, and from his [actual] home he has two thousand [cubits] in every direction, and he did not acquire anything beyond his eiruv. And due to this doubt, he is forbidden to walk [anywhere] except for the two thousand cubits between his home and his eiruv, since whichever way you look at it, within these [cubits] it is permitted; but the two thousand [cubits] from his eiruv and onward — no, lest he did not acquire [a residence through the] eiruv, and from his home and onward [in the opposite direction] also no, lest he did acquire [a residence through the] eiruv. It turns out that this [possibility] pulls him to walk here, and that [possibility] pulls him to walk there, like a person who leads a donkey and a camel, where the donkey walks ahead of him and he drives it [from behind], and the camel he pulls [from ahead], and he must turn [his attention both] ahead of him and behind him.

Rashi on Eruvin 35a:14:1.hebrew: הנותן את עירובו - הואיל ונתכוין לקנות שם שביתה, יש לו ארבע אמות. דהואיל והנהו ארבע אמות מיבלען בתחומא, הוו להו כתחומא, והוי כנותן את עירובו בבית שבסוף התחום — שאפילו הוא אלף אמה, מהלך את כולה וחוצה לה אלפים אמה:
Rashi on Eruvin 35a:14:1.english: One who places his eiruv - Since he intended to acquire [a place of] Shabbat residence there, he has four cubits. For since those four cubits are absorbed within the [city's Shabbat] limit, they become like the limit [itself], and it is as if he placed his eiruv in a house at the end of the limit — for even if it is a thousand cubits [long], he may walk all of it and [another] two thousand cubits beyond it.

Rashi on Eruvin 35a:15:1.hebrew: דאי בעי שקיל ליה - וקתני מתניתין אינו עירוב, משום טלטול אבנים — דשבות דרבנן הוא:
Rashi on Eruvin 35a:15:1.english: That if he wanted, he could take it - And the Mishnah teaches [that] it is not an eiruv because of handling stones, as it is a rabbinic prohibition [shevut].

Rashi on Eruvin 35a:1:1.english: However, on Shabbat, his eiruv is not [a valid] eiruv - For the Rabbis did not permit him to dismantle [it].

Rashi on Eruvin 35a:1:2.english: The key is found - On Shabbat.

Rashi on Eruvin 35a:1:3.hebrew: אין עירובו עירוב - דלית ליה דר"ש. והא דר"ש — בפ' כל גגות:
Rashi on Eruvin 35a:1:3.english: His eiruv is not a valid eiruv - For he does not hold in accordance with [the opinion of] Rabbi Shimon. And this [teaching] of Rabbi Shimon is in the chapter [entitled] Kol Gagot.

Rashi on Eruvin 35a:3:1.english: And there is no dismantling of utensils - And if he wishes, he may dismantle it.

Rashi on Eruvin 35a:4:1.english: Knocked - [A] zav [knocked] with his fist upon a carriage, etc.

Rashi on Eruvin 35a:4:2.hebrew: טמאים - מפני שהסיטן, וכגון שהיה לבוש בית יד, דלא מטמא בנגיעה; אי נמי, שהקישו בחתיכת עץ שבידו:
Rashi on Eruvin 35a:4:2.english: [They are] impure - Because he shifted them [imparting impurity through movement]; and [this is] for example where he was wearing a glove, so that he does not impart impurity through contact; or alternatively, where he struck it with a piece of wood in his hand.

Rashi on Eruvin 35a:5:1.english: It is a tent - And it does not contract ritual impurity.

Rashi on Eruvin 35a:6:1.hebrew: ותסברא - דטעמא משום אהל, ולאו אהל הוא:
Rashi on Eruvin 35a:6:1.english: And do you think [so] - That the reason is because of [it being] a tent, and it is not a tent?

Rashi on Eruvin 35a:6:2.hebrew: וניסט - שאינו תקוע יפה, וכשמקיש בו ניסט — טמא. ואם כלי הוא שמחובר ותקוע, או כבד הרבה שאינו ניסט מחמתו — טהור:
Rashi on Eruvin 35a:6:2.english: And it moved - [A tent] that is not fastened well, and when [the zav] knocks on it, it moves — [it is] impure. And if it is a utensil that is attached and fastened, or very heavy, so that it does not move on his account — [it is] pure.

Rashi on Eruvin 35a:6:3.hebrew: וקתני נמי סיפא - דקמייתא, דהקיש ע"ג שידה: אם היו ניסטין טמאין, אפילו לרבי נחמיה ור"ש — אלמא טעמייהו לאו משום אהל הוא:
Rashi on Eruvin 35a:6:3.english: And it also teaches in the latter clause - Of the first [teaching], that [stated]: “[If he] knocked upon a chest...”: If they were moved, they are impure, even according to Rabbi Neḥemya and Rabbi Shimon. Evidently, their reasoning is not because it is a tent.

Rashi on Eruvin 35a:6:4.hebrew: זה הכלל ניסט מחמת כחו - שהסיט את הכלי או את האהל ממש, שניתקו ממושבו משהו:
Rashi on Eruvin 35a:6:4.english: This is the principle: [If] it moved due to his force - That he moved the utensil or the tent directly, in that he dislodged it from its resting place [even] slightly.

Rashi on Eruvin 35a:6:5.hebrew: מחמת רעדה - שטפח ברגליו בקרקע, ומחמת ניענוע הקרקע ניסט הכלי — אף על פי שניתק מן הארץ — טהור, דכח כוחו הוא:
Rashi on Eruvin 35a:6:5.english: Due to vibrations - Where he stamped with his feet on the ground, and due to the shaking of the ground the utensil moved — even though it was displaced from the ground — [it is ritually] pure, for it is [merely] the force of his force [an indirect force].

Rashi on Eruvin 35a:7:1.hebrew: דכולי עלמא - אפילו לר' נחמיה, הסיט ממש מחמת כחו — טמא, ואפילו אהל:
Rashi on Eruvin 35a:7:1.english: All [agree] - Even according to Rabbi Neḥemya, actual movement caused by his force is impure, and even [in the case of] a tent.

Rashi on Eruvin 35a:7:2.english: [Movement] due to vibration [is] pure - And even if it is a utensil.

Rashi on Eruvin 35a:7:3.hebrew: והכא ברעדה מחמת כחו - שהקיש עליהן ממש, ולא נתקן ולא הוסטו, אלא רעדו:
Rashi on Eruvin 35a:7:3.english: And here, with vibration due to his force - That he struck directly upon them, and they were neither dislodged nor shifted, but rather vibrated:

Rashi on Eruvin 35a:8:1.hebrew: ומתני' - דעירוב, במאי מוקמינן לה? דהא לכ"ע: אי גדול הוא — אהל הוא, ואמאי עירובו עירוב? אי קטן, שאינו מחזיק מ' סאה בלח — כלי הוא, ומאי טעמא דר' אליעזר:
Rashi on Eruvin 35a:8:1.english: And the mishna - Regarding [the] eiruv, in what [case] do we establish it? For according to everyone, if it is large, it is a tent, and why is his eiruv a valid eiruv? If [it is] small, which does not hold forty se’ah in liquid, it is a utensil, and what is the reasoning of Rabbi Eliezer?

Rashi on Eruvin 35a:8:2.english: Tied with a cord - The lock is tied with a rope.

Rashi on Eruvin 35a:8:3.hebrew: ובעי סכינא למיפסקיה - דאי הוה מצי למיפסקיה בידיה שפיר דמי, אפי' לר' אליעזר, דאין חתיכה אסורה אלא במחובר; אבל הכא מקלקל הוא ושרי, כדתניא במסכת ביצה (דף לא:): חותמות שבכלים — מתיר ומפקיע וחותך. ואע"ג דהכא אהל הוא, ואמרינן התם: שבקרקע אסור לחתוך — גזירה דרבנן היא דמיחזי כסותר, ולא סותר בנין ממש הוא, דהא פתיחת דלת בעלמא הוא; כיון דשבות הוא, לא גזרו עליו בין השמשות:
Rashi on Eruvin 35a:8:3.english: And a knife is required to cut it - For if he had been able to cut it with his hands, it would be well [and permitted], even according to Rabbi Eliezer, as cutting is forbidden only in [the case of that which is] attached [to the ground]; but here, it is destructive, and [thus] permitted, as it is taught in tractate Beitzah (31b): With seals on vessels, one may untie, unravel, and cut. And even though here it is a tent, and we say there [that with seals] that are on the ground, it is forbidden to cut — that is a rabbinic decree, because it appears like dismantling [a building], but it is not actual dismantling of a structure, for it is merely opening a door; [and] since it is a rabbinic restriction [shevut], they did not decree against it during twilight.

Tosafot on Eruvin 35a:11:1.hebrew: נתגלגל חוץ לתחום - אפילו תחומין דרבנן, ואפילו לרבי דאמר: "כל דבר שהוא משום שבות לא גזרו עליו בין השמשות" — מכל מקום לא הוי עירוב. אף על גב דבין השמשות מצי למישקליה ואיתויי, כיון דאם קנה שביתה במקום שנתגלגל העירוב היה עומד עתה חוץ לתחום ואין לו אלא ארבע אמות — הילכך תקנו רבנן שלא יהיה עירוב אלא כשהוא בתוך התחום:
Tosafot on Eruvin 35a:11:1.english: [If it] rolled beyond the Shabbat limit - Even [if the prohibition of] Shabbat limits is rabbinic, and even according to Rebbi, who said: "Any matter that is [prohibited] on account of a shevut, they did not decree against it at twilight" — nevertheless, it is not a [valid] eiruv. Even though at twilight he is able to take it and bring it, since if he were to acquire [Shabbat] residence in the place where the eiruv rolled, he would now be standing outside the limit and have only four cubits; therefore, the Sages instituted that it is an eiruv only when it is within the limit.

Tosafot on Eruvin 35a:1:1.hebrew: חסורי מיחסרא והכי קתני - פ"ה: "וג' מחלוקות בדבר", ולא דק; דמתניתין איירי ביום טוב, ופליגי אי מצי סתר ליה אי לאו, וברייתא — כשנמצא בשבת, ופליגי בדר"ש. והא דתניא בתוספתא (פרק שני) דעירובין: "ומודים חכמים לרבי אליעזר בבני חצר ובני מרפסת שגבו עירובן ונתנוהו בבית, אע"פ שיודעין שאין המפתח במקומו, שעירובו עירוב" — היינו טעמא דבעירובי חצירות הקילו. ומיהו נראה דאנמצא מפתח בשבת קאי, מדקאמר: "ומודים חכמים לרבי אליעזר"; וביו"ט, כי לא נמצא מפתח, אדרבה, חכמים הקילו טפי, והוה ליה למימר איפכא: "ומודה רבי אליעזר לחכמים":
Tosafot on Eruvin 35a:1:1.english: The mishna is incomplete and it teaches the following - Rashi explained: "[There are] three disputes in this matter." But this is not precise, for the mishna is dealing with a Festival, and they dispute whether one can dismantle it or not; and the baraita [deals with a case] where [the key] was found on Shabbat, and they dispute concerning [the ruling] of Rabbi Shimon. And that which is taught in the Tosefta (chapter 2) of Eruvin: "And the Sages concede to Rabbi Eliezer regarding the residents of a courtyard and the residents of a balcony who collected their eiruv and placed it in a house, even though they know that the key is not in its place, that their eiruv is a valid eiruv" — the reason is that with eiruvei chatzerot they were lenient. However, it appears that [this baraita] refers to [a case where] the key was found on Shabbat, since it states: "And the Sages concede to Rabbi Eliezer"; whereas on a Festival, when the key is not found, on the contrary, the Sages were more lenient, and it should have stated the reverse: "And Rabbi Eliezer concedes to the Sages."

Tosafot on Eruvin 35a:1:2.hebrew: בעיר עירובו עירוב - בנמצא בשבת, אף על פי שהיה אבוד בין השמשות:
Tosafot on Eruvin 35a:1:2.english: In the city, his eiruv is a valid eiruv - [This refers to a case] where [the key] was found on Shabbat, even though it was lost at twilight.

Tosafot on Eruvin 35a:6:1.hebrew: וקתני סיפא אם היו ניסטין טמאין - מהך סיפא לחוד לא מצי למידק, דמצי למימר: דמחמת רעדה הוא דפליגי, דיש חלוק בין אהל לכלי, אבל בהיסט — אהל נמי טמא. לכך מייתי ברייתא, דמחמת רעדה נמי אין חילוק בין אהל לכלי. וברייתא לחוד נמי לא סגיא, דהוה אמינא דאתיא לא כרבי נחמיה ולא כרבי שמעון; להכי אייתי סיפא דמילתייהו:
Tosafot on Eruvin 35a:6:1.english: "And it teaches in the latter clause: If they moved, they are impure" - From this latter clause alone he could not deduce [this], for one could say that it is regarding [movement] due to vibration that they disagree, [holding] that there is a distinction between a tent and a utensil, but regarding [direct] movement, a tent is also impure. Therefore he brings the baraita, [which shows] that regarding [movement] due to vibration as well, there is no distinction between a tent and a utensil. And the baraita alone would also not suffice, for I would have said that it follows neither Rabbi Neḥemya nor Rabbi Shimon; therefore he brought the latter clause of their [own] statement.

Tosafot on Eruvin 35a:8:1.hebrew: ומתני' במאי מוקי ליה - ולא בעי לאוקומ' בפלוגתא דאין בנין בכלים, משום דפלוגתא דב"ש וב"ה היא בפרק ב' דביצה (ד' כב.):
Tosafot on Eruvin 35a:8:1.english: "And our Mishnah, how does he establish it?" - And the Gemara did not want to establish it as dependent on the dispute of "there is no building in vessels," because it is a dispute between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel in chapter 2 of Beitzah (22a).

Tosafot on Eruvin 35a:8:2.hebrew: בעי סכינא למיפסקיה - פ"ה: דאי ביד הוה שרי, אפילו רבי אליעזר, דמקלקל הוא; דתניא במסכת ביצה (דף לא:): "חותמות שבכלים מתיר ומפקיע וחותך". ואף על גב דהכא אהל הוא, ואמר שבקרקע אסור — גזירה דרבנן הוא דמיחזי כסותר, ולא סותר בנין ממש הוא, דהא פתיחת דלת בעלמא הוא; וכיון דשבות הוא, לא גזרו עליו בה"ש. ואינו נראה; דכי נמי סבר רבי אליעזר כרבי נחמיה — שרי, דטלטול סכין לא אסור אלא מדרבנן! לכך י"ל: דהכא כלי הוא, ואי הוה מצי למפסקיה ביד הוה שרי, אבל בסכינא אסור כרבי נחמיה, ולית ליה דרבי. ומכאן מדקדק ר"י: ד"חותמות שבכלים מתיר ומפקיע וחותך" היינו דוקא כעין קשר של מיתנא, אבל פותח של עץ או של מתכת אסור לשבר, דבכלי נמי יש בנין וסתירה, כדפ"ל:
Tosafot on Eruvin 35a:8:2.english: A knife is required to cut it - Rashi explained: For if [the strap could be severed] by hand, it would be permitted even according to Rabbi Eliezer, as he is causing damage [which is exempt on Shabbat]; as it was taught in a baraita in tractate Beitzah (31b): "One may untie, tear apart, or cut the seals on utensils." And even though here it is a tent [attached to the ground], and [the baraita] states that on the ground it is forbidden — that is a Rabbinic decree because it appears like dismantling, but it is not actual dismantling of a structure, for it is merely opening a door; and since it is a shevut, they did not decree against it at twilight. But this does not appear [correct]; for even if Rabbi Eliezer holds in accordance with Rabbi Neḥemya, it should be permitted, as moving a knife is forbidden only by Rabbinic law! Therefore, it must be said: Here [the cupboard] is a utensil, and if he were able to cut it by hand, it would be permitted; but with a knife it is forbidden in accordance with Rabbi Neḥemya, and [Rabbi Eliezer] does not accept [the view] of Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi, who holds that a shevut is not decreed at twilight]. And from here the Ri deduces: [The rule that] "one may untie, tear apart, or cut the seals on utensils" applies specifically to something like a knot of a strap, but a lock of wood or metal is forbidden to break, for in the case of a utensil as well, [the prohibitions of] building and dismantling apply, as was explained above.
